[[File:Great triakis icosahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a great triakis icosahedron]]
In [[geometry]], the '''great triakis icosahedron''' is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[uniform star polyhedron|uniform]] [[great stellated truncated dodecahedron]]. Its faces are isosceles triangles. Part of each triangle lies within the solid, hence is invisible in solid models.

== Proportions ==
The triangles have one angle of <math>\arccos(-\frac{3}{20}+\frac{3}{20}\sqrt{5})\approx 79.314\,951\,312\,25^{\circ}</math> and two of <math>\arccos(\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{20}\sqrt{5})\approx 50.342\,524\,343\,87^{\circ}</math>. The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(\frac{-24+15\sqrt{5}}{61})\approx 81.001\,410\,024\,84^{\circ}</math>.
